---
title: "Case study: weekly surveillance over many registries"
author: "[Richard Aubrey White](https://www.rwhite.no)"
---

A ministry of health holds many registries, with different formats, owners and delivery schedules. Surveillance runs the same analysis on all of them every week. In this case study, a registry is any source of surveillance data: a registry, a sentinel system or a notification system.

This case study shows a structure in three layers for this work. The Norwegian Institute of Public Health/Folkehelseinstituttet (NIPH/FHI) uses a version of it for its weekly respiratory surveillance.

## In production at FHI

FHI runs its respiratory surveillance trend analysis on this structure every week. The results go into the [weekly status reports on covid-19, influenza and other respiratory infections](https://www.fhi.no/publ/statusrapporter/luftveisinfeksjoner/). The code started in November 2023.

The pipeline uses 6 types of surveillance data from 7 registries. It uses an eighth registry when the newest hospital extract has it.

| Type of data | Registries |
|---|---|
| Consultations in general practice and emergency primary care | NorSySS |
| Outbreak notifications from health institutions | VESUV |
| Sentinel laboratory testing, tests and positive tests by pathogen | Fyrtårn |
| Laboratory-confirmed cases | Two registries: cases outside hospital, cases in hospital |
| Hospital admissions with severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) | All SARI admissions, and laboratory-positive SARI admissions when the extract has them |
| Deaths | The Norwegian Cause of Death Registry |

The registries arrive as delimited text files, Excel workbooks and R data files. Some give counts, and some give tests and positive tests. Some give the date each count was reported, and some do not. Each type of data gives one or more indicators, for example influenza and RSV from the laboratory.

One function for each registry converts its data to a table that follows one data contract. One pipeline then runs the same methods on every indicator.

## Three layers

| Layer | Holds | Owner | Article |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registry packages | One package for each registry. It reads the raw data and returns a table that follows the data contract. | The registry team | [1. A contract for each registry](case-study-contract.html) |
| Methods packages | The surveillance methods: nowcasting, trends and intensity levels. They read tables that follow the data contract. | The methods team | [2. The methods are in packages](case-study-methods.html) |
| The pipeline | One plnr plan. It runs the methods on every indicator of every registry. Later plans make the tables, figures and report. | The surveillance team | [3. One pipeline over every registry](case-study-pipeline.html) |

At FHI, the registry functions are part of the pipeline code, one function for each registry. This case study puts each function in its own registry package. The team that owns a registry then also owns the code that reads it.

FHI's methods are in the methods package [csalert](https://niphr.github.io/csalert/), which article 2 runs.

## What the structure gives a ministry

- **A new registry needs one package and one line.** The package returns a table that follows the contract. The pipeline needs one `add_data()` call, and reads the indicators and locations from the data.
- **A method change applies to every indicator.** The next run uses the changed method for every indicator of every registry, with no change to the pipeline.
- **Broken data stops the run before the report.** The pipeline checks the contract each time it loads a registry. The error names the registry and every rule it breaks.
- **Each team works on its own layer.** The registry team does not need to understand the methods. The methods team does not need to read the raw formats.
- **One results format.** The analysis of every indicator returns the same columns, so one table and one figure show every registry.

The three articles run on synthetic data. The code on each page runs as written, and the page shows its output.
